description:
How Did the Universe Grow Faster Than Light?

Episode 113 of a daily journey through the universe. 💥
We go back to the first trillionth of a trillionth of a trillionth of a second: cosmic inflation, when the universe may have grown from smaller than an atom to about the size of a grapefruit, why space itself can stretch faster than light, and the clues left in the oldest light.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 114: Next stop, the Hubble tension. Scientists can't agree how fast the universe is growing.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #bigbang #astronomy #shorts #science #nasa

segments.text: How could the universe grow faster than light? It happened in a split second.
In episode twenty-three, we went back to the Big Bang. Now we go back even further, to the very first instant.
segments.headline: Back to the first instant

segments.text: Many scientists think that in the first tiny fraction of a second, the universe grew incredibly fast. It's called inflation.
In much less than a blink, a region smaller than an atom may have grown to the size of a grapefruit.
segments.headline: Atom to grapefruit

segments.text: Wait, faster than light? Nothing can travel through space faster than light. But space itself can stretch faster.
Inflation explains why the universe looks so smooth in every direction, and so flat.
segments.headline: Why so smooth?

segments.text: Tiny ripples from that moment grew into the seeds of galaxies. Every galaxy you see started as a quantum wiggle.
segments.headline: Seeds of galaxies

segments.text: We see the pattern of those ripples in the oldest light in the universe, the cosmic microwave background.
segments.headline: Clues in the oldest light

segments.text: Inflation isn't proven yet. Scientists are hunting for its gravitational waves to be sure.
segments.headline: The hunt continues

segments.text: Tomorrow, a mystery that's driving scientists crazy. Two ways of measuring how fast the universe grows, and they don't agree. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
